## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

The core challenge is capturing proteasome inhibitor-specific tolerability alongside disease burden preservation in a global registration trial requiring both regulatory credibility and HTA utility data.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

| Fatigue | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-MY20, PRO-CTCAE, FACT-G | EORTC QLQ-C30 ⚠️ General (no MM module) | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |

## Key Observations

• **PRO-CTCAE has explicit FDA endorsement**: FDA's 2024 Core PRO Guidance names PRO-CTCAE as "an example of one acceptable item library for assessment of symptomatic adverse events" [IR-002] — the strongest regulatory endorsement of any item library approach for capturing treatment tolerability in oncology.

• **Item library approach precedent established**: TOURMALINE-MM1 used subscales rather than full EORTC instruments, reducing burden while achieving regulatory acceptance [TI-001]. This calibrated SOA approach aligns with your proteasome inhibitor comparator and reduces total administration time significantly.

• **Missing utility data is a registration risk**: Only 2 of 5 comparator trials collected utility measures [TI-002, TI-004], but both NICE and ICER require EQ-5D-5L for cost-effectiveness evaluation — without this, UK market access is severely compromised and US value assessment is limited.

• **Endpoint positioning strongly favors secondary**: In 21 KG MM trials, 71% positioned PRO as secondary endpoints with 0% as primary [PRO endpoint positioning]. This suggests PRO should be positioned as key secondary within a hierarchical testing strategy anchored by PFS.

• **Peripheral neuropathy gap identified**: Domain coverage matrix shows no candidate instrument for peripheral neuropathy burden — a critical oversight given proteasome inhibitor mechanism and bortezomib class precedent requiring CIPN monitoring as shown in BOSTON trial [TI-005].

• **Multiplicity control failures are a major rejection driver**: Multiple KG rejection records cite "no alpha-control," "not in testing hierarchy," and "no multiplicity adjustment" as primary FDA rejection reasons [REJ-019, REJ-020, REJ-031, REJ-032, REJ-039] — pre-specification within a controlled testing sequence is non-negotiable.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In candidate list? | Action needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes (proposed addition) | Include in battery — mandatory for UK reimbursement |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L (preferred) | Yes (proposed addition) | Include in battery — critical for US value assessment |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Whether to implement calibrated SOA approach** for EORTC instruments following TOURMALINE-MM1 precedent to reduce patient burden while maintaining regulatory acceptability.

2. **How to address peripheral neuropathy assessment gap** — consider adding EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 or PRO-CTCAE neuropathy items given proteasome inhibitor mechanism.

3. **Hierarchical testing sequence positioning** — confirm PRO endpoints sit below PFS in testing hierarchy consistent with 71% secondary positioning pattern in MM trials.

4. **PRO-CTCAE item selection strategy** — determine specific symptomatic AE items aligned with proteasome inhibitor safety profile and FDA Core PRO domain requirements.

5. **Assessment schedule optimization** — balance frequent early timepoints to capture treatment tolerability against late timepoints for sustained benefit evaluation in the global regulatory submission.
